title: 1987 AHSME Problem 3
statement: How many primes less than \(100\) have \(7\) as the ones digit? (Assume the usual base \(10\) representation.)

solutions.text:
The primes are \[ 7,\ 17,\ 37,\ 47,\ 67,\ 97. \] The other candidates are composite: \(27,57,77,\) and \(87.\) Hence there are \(6\) such primes.

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: List every positive integer below \(100\) whose ones digit is \(7\)
For numbers below \(100,\) trial division only requires primes through their square roots
